label: Thomas Aquinas, In octo libros Physicorum…: A second mover moves not by its own power but because…
locator: VIII, lect. 9 nn. 1038-1039: the second mover cannot cause motion independently of the first
interpretation: A second mover moves 'not on its own account, i.e., not by its own power, but because it has been moved by some other mover'; the first mover is more a mover, because it moves the second and because 'the second mover cannot cause motion independently of the first, but the first can cause it independently of the second' (stick, hand, man). Read as defining a second mover by the dependence of its moving on its being moved. Like SCG I.13 [15], it does not address a mover moved only in a respect irrelevant to its moving. Basis: the English translation named in the passage manifest; a candidate for upgrade once a pinned Latin witness exists, and never a ground for overriding a reading of the Leonine/SCTA Latin.
